page: Amazon Web Services c6i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine instance running on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. Powered by Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C processors based on the x86_64 architecture, the server provides 32 dedicated vCPUs across 16 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading at a clock frequency of 3.5 GHz. The processor package includes 54 MB of shared L3 cache and supports instruction sets including AVX-512 with VNNI, AES, and SHA extensions. Memory capacity is configured at 64.0 GB of DDR4 RAM running at 3 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU.

The instance does not include integrated local disk storage or hardware accelerators such as GPUs, relying on network-attached storage over an architecture configured with a 12 Gbps baseline network bandwidth profile. Memory bandwidth evaluations demonstrate read throughput of 147.98 GB/sec and write throughput of 66.82 GB/sec on uncached 256 MB blocks, along with 1,661.16 GB/sec cached read throughput.

Benchmark results show balanced compute performance, recording 30,975.47 on stress-ng multi-core and 13,945.0 on Geekbench multi-core. Specialized operations reflect high processing capacity, including a Clang software compilation score of 26,609.0, static web serving throughput of 35.25 GB/sec, and 31.19 million Redis SET operations per second. LLM inference benchmarks show strong results on small 135M models at 303.91 tokens/sec for text generation, but drop to 6.2 tokens/sec for 70B prompt processing due to the absence of dedicated tensor acceleration hardware.

By omitting local storage arrays and surplus memory capacity, c6i.8xlarge provides an efficient compute profile for CPU-dominated execution pipelines. The platform is best fitted for continuous integration build clusters, parallel scientific computing, web application serving, batch processing tasks, and distributed analytics workers.
description: Amazon Web Services c6i.8xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, utilizing 3rd Generation Intel Xeon 8375C processors. It provides 32 vCPUs across 16 physical cores operating at 3.5 GHz, supported by 64.0 GB of DDR4 memory at a compute-focused 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio. The server lacks local instance storage and dedicated GPU hardware, operating with a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps. Computational testing highlights reliable performance across compute workloads, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 13,945.0, static web throughput of 35.25 GB/sec, and 31.19 million Redis SET operations per second. Small-model LLM generation reaches 303.91 tokens/sec, though performance scales down for larger models due to the absence of hardware accelerators. This configuration provides a resource-dense compute footprint for distributed batch processing, CI/CD compilation pipelines, web server fleets, and parallel scientific calculations.
